label: SDRplay (RSP1A / RSPdx / RSPduo)
gain_description: Master driver-gain element. Wire convention: higher value = more received signal (`SoapySource` inverts at the boundary for SDRplay's reduction-shaped element, so the operator/UI/CLI all agree on "high = loud"). Range 0–66 on the dial. The driver spends the reduction on IFGR first (IF gain reduction, 20–59 dB, real dB) and the rest on RFGR, which is the LNA *state* index (0–27 on the RSPdx, 0–9 on RSP1A/RSP1B/RSPduo, 0–8 on RSP2, 0–3 on RSP1): dial ≥ 27 → RFGR 0 and IFGR = 86 − dial; dial < 27 → IFGR 59 and RFGR = 27 − dial. An LNA state is not a dB value — each band has its own attenuator ladder (RSPdx: state 4 = 12 dB below 50 MHz, state 7 = 27 dB at 60–250 MHz, state 1 = 7 dB at 420–1000 MHz) — so the readback reports it separately as `lna` and its `gain_db` is true dB (`dial_db` is the dial position). The separate `rfgain_sel` setting writes the LNA state directly and is still attenuation-shaped (lower index = less attenuation = louder); see its own tooltip.

rfgain_sel.label: LNA attenuation
rfgain_sel.description: Front-end LNA-state index: 0–27 on the RSPdx (fewer valid states per band: 19 below 12 MHz, 20 at 12–50 MHz, 25 at 50–60, 27 at 60–250, 28 at 250–420, 21 at 420–1000, 19 above 1 GHz), 0–9 on RSP1A/RSP1B/RSPduo. 0 = no attenuation (maximum gain); higher values insert attenuator stages whose dB amount depends on the frequency band (the SDRplay API spec gain tables — the readback's `lna.atten_db` shows the value in force). State 4 ≈ 12 dB at HF/MW (measured 8–14 dB), enough to bury weak HF signals (FT8 / WSPR / SSB DX); set to 0 for HF reception. The `gain_db` dial also sets this state (dial < 27 → state 27 − dial) and a later dial write overrides an explicit value here. Despite the upstream SoapySDRPlay3 label of 'RF Gain Select', this is an attenuator index, not a gain knob — lower is louder.

rfnotch_ctrl.label: AM/FM broadcast notch
rfnotch_ctrl.description: RSPdx hardware notch covering AM (540–1.7 MHz) + FM (88–108 MHz) broadcast bands. Default ON to keep strong locals out when receiving away from those bands; auto-disabled when the centre is inside AM or FM.

dabnotch_ctrl.label: DAB Band III notch
dabnotch_ctrl.description: RSPdx hardware notch over DAB Band III (170–240 MHz). Default ON; auto-disabled when the centre is inside Band III.

hdr_ctrl.label: HDR mode (≤ 2 MHz only)
hdr_ctrl.description: RSPdx high-dynamic-range mode for the LF/MW bands below 2 MHz. Has no effect above 2 MHz; safe to leave default-ON.

biasT_ctrl.label: Bias-T (DC on antenna)
biasT_ctrl.description: Applies +4.7 V DC on the antenna port for active LNAs / preamps. Default OFF — turn ON only when the connected antenna explicitly needs it.

notes: IF filter picked as the largest ladder entry ≤ Fs. SDRplay's own default of 200 kHz brick-walls the spectrum at ±100 kHz, and any filter wider than Fs makes the driver silently upclock Fs — so we pick from the ladder explicitly rather than leaving it to the driver. Advertised max of 10.66 MS/s fails activateStream in practice; clamped to 10 MS/s. `rfgain_sel` is exposed (with a clarifying label override) since the upstream SoapySDR label calls it a gain knob but it's actually an LNA attenuator index (0–27 on the RSPdx) — leaving it at 4 costs ≈ 12 dB on HF/MW (the API ladder; measured 8–14 dB), which hid weak signals. The readback reports the state separately (`lna`) instead of counting the index as dB.
ai_operator_notes:
SDRplay **RSPdx** — 14-bit single-tuner SDR, 1 kHz – 2 GHz. Sample rates: the decimated ladder 62.5 k / 96 k / 125 k / 192 k / 250 k / 384 k / 500 k / 768 k / 1 MS/s, then any rate from 2 to 10 MS/s (the API advertises 10.66 but `activateStream` fails above 10, so the daemon clamps there); 0.25–10 MS/s verified drop-free over SoapyRemote on 2026-10-12. Analog filters 200 k / 300 k / 600 k / 1.536 M / 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 MHz, picked as the largest ≤ rate — at 2.4 MS/s the filter is **1.536 MHz, so only ±0.77 MHz of the span is real**; at 0.5 / 0.25 MS/s it is 300 k / 200 k, narrower than a 240 kHz wbfm channel plus any DC dodge (see the DC spike section). Keep the preset-declared 2.4 MS/s for surveys and decoders (their channelizers are exact there) and reach for 6–10 MS/s when hunting across a band. Three antenna ports — pick the one that matches the band you're tuning before debugging anything else.

### Antennas

- **Antenna A** — SMA, full 1 kHz – 2 GHz range. General-purpose for VHF / UHF with a whip / discone / dipole. Default for >30 MHz when the operator hasn't said otherwise.
- **Antenna B** — SMA, full 1 kHz – 2 GHz range, with **Bias-T (4.7 V DC)** available. Use for an active antenna / preamp that needs power; flip `biasT_ctrl=true` only then.
- **Antenna C** — **BNC high-impedance input, 1 kHz – 200 MHz, optimized for HF / MW / LW.** Best port for shortwave SWL, AM broadcast, FT8 / WSPR, NDBs, ham HF bands. For anything below 30 MHz this is usually the right choice; for VHF up to ~200 MHz it works but A/B are usually better.

If you don't know what the operator has hooked to which port, **read the `Operator-supplied radio setup` section** below. If it isn't filled in, *say so* ("I don't know what's on Antenna B — can you tell me?") rather than cycling antennas blind.

### Gain — two stages

`--gain N` (and the UI slider) means **N dB of received-signal gain — higher = louder**. Range 0–66. The daemon inverts under the hood when the driver advertises gain-reduction units (SDRplay does), so the CLI / UI / wire all agree on the same convention.

Two physical stages under the master knob:

1. **IFGR** (IF gain reduction, 20–59 dB) — controlled by AGC OR manual; never both. `ferrite-ctl tune --gain N` atomically sets `agc=false` in the same PATCH, so manual gain just works. If you *want* AGC instead, pass no `--gain` flag and leave `agc=true`.
2. **LNAstate / RFGR** (`rfgain_sel`, LNA state index — 0–27 on the RSPdx, with fewer valid states in most bands; each state is a band-dependent attenuation step from the SDRplay API tables, e.g. state 4 = 12 dB at HF/MW (measured 8–14 dB), state 7 = 27 dB at 60–250 MHz) — *always* manual, separate from AGC. This is the only knob that's still attenuation-shaped: **lower index = less attenuation = louder.**

**The `gain_db` dial sets the LNA state itself**, deterministically: dial ≥ 27 → RFGR 0 and IFGR = 86 − dial (40 → IFGR 46); dial < 27 → IFGR 59 and RFGR = 27 − dial (20 → RFGR 7, 25 → RFGR 2). An explicit `rfgain_sel` restarts the source, stays in `settings` across retunes and restarts, and the next `gain_db` write overrides it (the write reply says so) — clear it with `settings {"rfgain_sel": null}` when done (`settings {}` is a no-op: settings merge per key). `source_readback` reports the LNA state separately as `lna` (`state`, `states`, `atten_db` from the per-band ladder, `band_hz`); its `gain_db` is true dB with the state counted at that attenuation, and `dial_db` is the dial position. Dial 20 at 118 MHz therefore reads back `dial_db 20, lna.state 7, lna.atten_db 27, gain_db 0` — 66 dB of reduction from the loudest setting.

```
ferrite-ctl --note "max LNA gain for weak HF" param src settings='{"rfgain_sel":"0"}'
```

Gain decision tree (measured on this station 2026-10-12, all values `gain_db`, `agc=false` unless stated; confirm with `source_readback`):
- HF < 30 MHz → **gain 40** (IFGR 46 / RFGR 0); 35 when big broadcasters are in band. 50 only lifts the floor, 60 overloads, MW on the longwire overloads at 50. **Do not use AGC on HF** — it runs to gain 60–65 and overloads.
- 88–150 MHz → **needs RFGR ≥ 2 (dial ≤ 25)**: with RFGR 0 the LNA overloads (floor +30–50 dB, stations vanish, intermod lines such as 127.930 MHz). **gain 20** (RFGR 7) for airband and 2 m — the product is the receiver's own front end, the same on every antenna, and an FM bandstop does not change the 118–150 MHz threshold. FM broadcast: gain 25 (RFGR 2) — **except on an antenna port with an FM bandstop in line (this station: Antenna A), which is clean at RFGR 0 up to gain 50** while the unfiltered ports (B, C) still overload at 40. AGC never moves RFGR, so it cannot help. In the FM band, 2.2–3.0 MS/s with RFGR 0 also returns a flat −58 dBFS floor; 2.0 or ≥ 6 MS/s are fine.
- 162 MHz → gain 35. 400–450 MHz → gain 40. 460 MHz–2 GHz → **gain 50**; AGC lands at 51–66 there and is acceptable.
- Overload check at any band: step the gain 10 dB — if the floor rises ≈ 10 dB and no peak gains SNR, you are antenna-noise-limited (fine); if the floor jumps 30+ dB or peaks disappear, back off until RFGR ≥ 2.

When the explorer-prompt gain-calibration loop says "escalate after `--gain` alone has plateaued," check `source_readback` first: if RFGR is already 0 there is nothing left to escalate, and on HF the plateau means antenna noise, not a deaf receiver.


### Hardware notches — auto-toggled by UI

The daemon auto-toggles the per-band notches based on the centre frequency (server-side source policy, applied identically for the UI, ferrite-ctl, and a headless AI). You don't need to manage them unless you have a specific reason:

- `rfnotch_ctrl` — AM (540 kHz – 1.7 MHz) + FM broadcast (88 – 108 MHz). Default ON for intermod rejection; auto-disabled inside those bands.
- `dabnotch_ctrl` — DAB Band III (170 – 240 MHz). Default ON; auto-disabled inside.
- `hdr_ctrl` — HDR mode for LF/MW (below 2 MHz). Default ON; no effect above 2 MHz. Safe to leave on.
- `biasT_ctrl` — DC bias on Antenna B only. Default OFF — turn ON only when the connected antenna explicitly needs it.

### DC spike — zero-IF leakage

The RSPdx is **zero-IF above ~30 MHz** (and low-IF below — no spike in HF). At zero-IF the local oscillator leaks straight through to the ADC, producing a constant bright vertical line at the *tuned centre*. If you park the centre on your target, the spike obliterates it.

**Primary fix on SDRplay: `dc_offset_correction` (the `dc` toggle next to `agc` in the quick bar / input panel, or `param src dc_offset_correction=true`).** SDRplay's driver implements automatic DC-offset tracking, so leaving this ON (the default) suppresses the spike at the analog/early-DSP stage — you can then tune on-target. It's live-tunable, no rebuild. Only turn it OFF for a diagnostic A/B or when a signal sitting exactly at carrier is being eaten by the tracker. On top of the tracker, the `tune` verb applies an automatic DC dodge (`tune_offset_ratio` 0.7): it parks the source LO off-target by ~0.7× the channel rate so the spike falls outside the demodulated channel, then the channelizer pulls the signal back to baseband. The dodge is clamped to the analog passband, so it shrinks at low sample rates (0.5 MS/s, 300 kHz filter: 30 kHz for a 240 kHz channel; 0.25 MS/s: none — the channel is wider than the filter) and `health.issues` names a channel that still reaches past the filter edge (`tuning.passband_hz` / `chan_rate_hz`). So even with the tracker off, on-target tuning never leaves a signal sitting on the spike — the two mechanisms are complementary. Below 30 MHz on the RSPdx the spike isn't there regardless.

### Internal spurs — every multiple of 24 MHz (RSPdx)

This station's RSPdx shows **internal reference spurs at exact multiples of 24 MHz** (72, 96, 120 … 360, 408, 432 … 1536, 1656, 1680 MHz; 44 of the 70 harmonics from 72 MHz to 1.68 GHz). They are the receiver's own 24 MHz reference leaking into its receive path, not signals and not on-site RFI: measured 2026-10-16 they sit exactly on frequency against the radio's own clock (≤ 0.004 ppm), are ~5 Hz wide and steady, and are just as strong on a 50 Ω-terminated port as on an antenna; a USB ferrite does nothing. Treat a narrow, steady line at n × 24 MHz as a spur: don't report it, don't tune to it, and don't chase it with antenna changes. The emitter list already carries them as `ignored` ("RSPdx internal spur: 24 MHz reference ×N"). Only a 24 MHz multiple that is *modulated*, wide, or keyed is worth a second look.

### Driver warnings — what to expect under `tail decoder --category driver`

Not every failure surfaces in the HTTP response body. ferrited captures Soapy + libsdrplay log output under `tracing` target `driver`, so `ferrite-ctl tail decoder --category driver --lookback 30` shows everything the driver emitted in the last 30 seconds.

Messages you'll meet:

- `Not updating IFGR gain because AGC is enabled` — your `--gain N` was silently ignored. **Stop, disable AGC, redo the tune.** Don't paper over by adjusting elsewhere — the gain you intended hasn't landed and your captures are at AGC's pick, not yours.
- `sdrplay_api_Update(Tuner_Gr) Error: sdrplay_api_OutOfRange` — related symptom of the AGC-vs-manual conflict, or an actual out-of-range gain-reduction value (1–59 for IFGR).
- `sdrplay_api_Update(Tuner_FrF) Error: sdrplay_api_OutOfRange` — tune frequency genuinely out of range, or a driver state-transition glitch (rare; usually self-clears on the next tune).
- `U` / `O` SSI (under `driver::ssi`) — stream underflow / overflow. Steady underflows mean the SDR isn't keeping up with the requested sample rate; overflows mean ferrited's pipeline can't drain fast enough. Spot-check, not a per-tune blocker.

Flag any persistent driver warning (same message after a clean retry) with `[REVIEW]` so the user can see it's a tool-side problem, not operator skill.
